The numbers

Same tax rate, same neighborhood

Three properties in tax rate area 00067, all taxed at 1.18738 percent. A single-family home at 530 S Mapleton Dr pays $436,006 on 1.29 acres. The Los Angeles Country Club pays $285,533 on 308 acres.

Why the taxes are so low

Westfield Century City

$13,993,870

on 42 acres, assessed at $1.18B. Twelve private clubs pay, all together, about a quarter of that.

A parcel tax, explained

Why the taxes are so low

Proposition 13 (1978)

Land a club has owned since before 1975 is still valued from its 1975 figure plus small annual increases. Member-owned clubs almost never sell, so they almost never reset.

Learn more →

The 1960 golf-course rule

Nonprofit golf courses of ten acres or more are assessed on their use as golf courses, not on what the land would be worth for anything else.

Learn more →

The 1985 court case

In Los Angeles Country Club v. Pope, the Court of Appeal held the clubs get the benefit of both rules at once. That remains the law.

Learn more →

Twelve private clubs sit on three square miles of the most valuable land in America and pay, all together, about a quarter of what the Century City mall pays.
